NOTE ON FORMAT: OpenClaw nests servers under `mcp.servers`, NOT the
`mcpServers` key used by Claude Desktop and most other MCP clients, and it
keeps them inside its single config file (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) rather
than a standalone file. Both shapes are shown below.
Prefer the CLI over hand-editing openclaw.json — it validates the entry and
probes the server before saving. See _openclaw_cli.
Merge this into ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. Verified against OpenClaw
2026.7.1-2 on Windows: `openclaw mcp probe unifi-monitor` reports 11 tools.
`enabled` is optional and defaults to true; the CLI omits it when adding.
Use an absolute interpreter path — a gateway-launched process does not
necessarily inherit the PATH that resolves a bare `python`.

_openclaw_cli: openclaw mcp probe unifi-monitor    # confirms 11 tools
openclaw mcp reload                 # pick up config changes without a restart

_comment: Claude Desktop and most other MCP clients use this shape in their own
config file. POSIX paths shown; on Windows use the values above.

_note_on_credentials: The gateway side needs no controller credentials at all — only the path
to the SQLite file. That is the point of the split: a compromised or
malfunctioning model cannot reach the network, only the record of it.
UNIFI_DB_PATH must be set here rather than left to the env file: the MCP
server is launched by the gateway, not from a shell.
